newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West spot down ahead of holiday, warm weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West spot down ahead of holiday, warm weather.

text.p: Spot power prices in the western U.S. fell ahead of weaker demand related to the Christmas holiday on Wednesday as well as warmer regional temperatures, trade sources said Monday.
"The holiday seems to be a big factor here, a lot of businesses will also be closed on Tuesday or Thursday," said one trader.
In addition, many utilities will be shut Tuesday, so electricity deliveries are being pre-scheduled through Thursday.
The Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) on Monday offered prices through Thursday at $9.00 to $10.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) below previous offers.
"A lot of utilities are in sell mode. Hydroelectric supplies are plentiful," said another trader.
He noted that a cold front forecast for later this week is now seen overshooting the Pacific Northwest, hitting mainly the central U.S.
"Unless that cold front shifts, we could see lower prices for Friday," the trader added.
Firm, peak electricity at the California-Oregon border (COB) for Tuesday through Thursday was last quoted $19.00-21.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), compared with $27.00-28.00 for Monday.
Firm, off-peak COB power for Tuesday-Thursday was also lower at $14.00-15.00.
Next-day firm, peak power at Mid-Columbia (Mid-C) was pegged at $18.00-$20.00, compared with $26.00-28.00 on Friday.
COB for first-quarter 1997 was last quoted $18.60-18.90, while second quarter was quoted $12.90-13.25.
Palo Verde (PV) for first quarter was heard done at $20.75, while third-quarter was reported to trade at $24.60.
Firm, peak Palo Verde (PV) electricity for Tuesday-Thursday was quoted $21.00-22.00, compared with $25.00-26.00.
Off-peak PV for firm delivery Tuesday-Thursday was quoted near $15.00.
Next-day firm, peak prices at Four Corners were in line with PV at around $22.00. Firm, off-peak Four Corners power was assessed at $15.00-16.00.
